metadata.title: The Graduation That Opened the Sky

setup.pitch: Ninefold Academy's graduation ends by lighting nine capstone beacons that seal the school's sky observatory for another year. This year one capstone was erased from the ceremony—and the ninth beacon opens the sky instead.
setup.gmSummary: Ninefold Academy's commencement ritual is not merely ceremonial. Nine student capstones are selected each year to provide the ward concepts that close and recalibrate the academy's planar observatory. This year Provost Halden Vey removed expelled student Mira Sol's capstone on grounding unstable portals after she accused a senior professor of plagiarizing her work. Halden substituted an impressive but incomplete faculty demonstration. When the ninth beacon ignites, the observatory tears open into the Astral Sea and fragments of unfinished student magic spill across campus. The party must learn what was omitted, recover Mira's grounding work or reconstruct it independently, stabilize students and faculty, and decide whether the academy restores Mira's capstone, rewrites the graduation ward process under independent oversight, or permanently disconnects the observatory from the commencement rite.
setup.background: The Ninefold ceremony began as a practical peer-review safeguard: no observatory cycle closed until nine different students' work had been tested against the ward system. Over generations, the ritual became prestigious theater. Halden treated the capstones as symbolic slots rather than functional checks. Mira's project specifically modeled failure cascades when one ward concept is missing. Removing it created exactly the condition she warned about.
setup.campaignFrame: Joss Amber escorts Hearthford apprentices to Ninefold Academy's commencement and notices that the ninth beacon mount does not match the floor channel beneath it. She pulls the party into the investigation, and they return to Hearthford with Joss remembering whether they fixed the institution as well as the machinery.

quest.objective: Stabilize the campus, discover why the ninth beacon failed, recover or reconstruct the missing grounding capstone, and decide how Ninefold Academy closes the planar breach.
quest.stakes: The observatory is opening into the Astral Sea, student projects are manifesting physically, and the academy's credibility depends on whether it acknowledges the omitted work or hides the cause.
quest.deadline: NINE BEACONS: show nine marks. Six are lit at start. Fill one after commencement court, capstone hall, archive/lab, and observatory approach; beacon nine begins the finale breach. At nine unresolved, planar pressure escalates each round.
successConditions: The missing grounding concept is recovered or independently reconstructed.
Students and civilians are cleared from the observatory danger zone.
The breach is resolved through Restore, Reform, or Disconnect.
failureConditions: The party abandons the campus while the breach continues expanding.
The observatory is destroyed without securing the students trapped in its projection chambers.

facts.text: The nine capstones are functional peer-review ward inputs, not ceremonial decorations.
Provost Halden removed Mira Sol's grounding capstone after her expulsion and substituted an incomplete faculty demonstration.
Mira's expulsion followed her accusation that Professor Orien Pell copied her portal-stability work into a faculty paper.
The planar breach expands because the ward cycle lacks a grounding model; any valid grounding solution can stabilize it, not only Mira personally.
The crisis can end by restoring Mira's capstone, reforming the ward process under independent review, or disconnecting the observatory from the commencement beacons.

secrets.text: Halden knowingly inserted Orien Pell's demonstration into Mira's capstone slot to avoid reopening the plagiarism dispute.

secrets.text: A complete copy of Mira's grounding model survives in three places: her expelled-student locker, the archive version history, and a student study group's copied notes.

scenes.title: The Ninth Beacon Opens
scenes.purpose: Launch the planar breach, establish the beacon clock, and show that one graduation slot is wrong.
scenes.readAloud: Eight beacons burn steady around the graduation court. The ninth ignites—and the sky above Ninefold Academy opens like a silver eye. Graduation caps lift into the air. A tower window reflects stars that are not in this world. On beacon nine, the student nameplate has been replaced by a polished faculty crest.
gmNotes: Show NINE BEACONS with marks 1–6 already filled; fill 7/9 when the party leaves the court.
The breach is planar and anchored to academy wards, so simple flight or teleportation can reposition characters but does not close it.
DC 15 Arcana or Investigation identifies the ninth beacon as a mismatched ward input. Failure changes nothing; physical sigils and Capstone Hall make the mismatch obvious.
Halden authorizes campus access because projection labs are beginning to fail.
Send the party to Capstone Hall before assuming an external planar attack.

scenes.readAloud: Eight student bays hum in different colors. The ninth holds an elegant faculty portal model—but its brass base does not fit the floor channel beneath it. At the edge of the bay, someone scraped away a name hard enough to gouge the wood: MIRA SOL.
gmNotes: Fill beacon 8/9 when this scene ends.
DC 15 Arcana identifies the demonstration's missing grounding term. Failure gives no false equation; archive version history and study notes remain available.
Search reveals three recovery leads: Mira's expelled-student locker, archive version history, and study-group copy in Projection Labs.
A magical copy spell or divination can speed retrieval, but authorship and process evidence still matter for the Reform route.
Manifested capstone fragments begin appearing in Projection Labs, creating rescue pressure.

scenes.title: Version History
scenes.purpose: Establish authorship, Halden's approval, and a complete reconstructable grounding model.
scenes.readAloud: The Ward Archive keeps every change. Lines of luminous script hover above crystal ledgers: student drafts, faculty imports, beacon assignments, disciplinary orders. One sequence is impossible to miss. MIRA SOL — GROUNDING MODEL. Exported. Removed. Imported into ORIEN PELL — STABILITY NOTES.
gmNotes: Do not advance beacon nine yet; this scene is preparation before the final ignition.

DC 15 Investigation/Arcana reconstructs a usable grounding model from version history. Failure means the model is incomplete until one additional source is added from Mira's locker or study-group notes.
Halden's signed beacon substitution and Orien's import history are independent evidence.
High-level divinations can reveal authorship faster, but the physical/version records remain necessary if the academy later disputes it.
Once a valid model exists, the party can use it to stabilize one Projection Lab ward automatically.

scenes.title: Eight Projects Running Loose
scenes.purpose: Give Level 9 characters meaningful rescue work and prove the grounding solution before the observatory finale.
scenes.readAloud: The Projection Labs have become eight different emergencies at once: a gravity room turned sideways, animated sculpture blocking an exit, a pocket forest growing through stone, and students trapped behind glassy ward panes while silver stars leak through every crack.
gmNotes: Run three rescue jobs: trapped students, runaway project, unstable ward pane. High-level spells can solve jobs automatically if they clearly address the problem; reward capability rather than invalidating it.
Without a fitting spell, each job uses DC 15 Arcana/Athletics/Investigation or another justified skill. Failure adds one PLANAR PRESSURE mark but the job remains solvable another way.
Using the reconstructed grounding model on any ward pane proves it works and grants one prepared Restore success in the finale.
If Mira is found through Sending, divination, teleportation, or ordinary search, she can assist but is not required.
When three jobs resolve, beacon nine begins final ignition and the observatory becomes the only remaining unstable node.

scenes.title: Ground, Reform, or Sever
scenes.purpose: Resolve the planar crisis through correct ward input, institutional redesign, or permanent disconnection.
scenes.readAloud: Beacon nine flares. The observatory dome turns transparent, revealing the Astral Sea directly overhead. Nine ward pylons circle the aperture. Eight burn with student sigils. The ninth is a blank white fire. Three controls rise from the central ring: RESTORE. REVIEW. DISCONNECT. In the breach, an equation-shaped figure turns toward you. “Eight known. Ninth unresolved.”
gmNotes: Ninth Echo starts AC 16, 96 HP. PLANAR PRESSURE adds one minor Echo Fragment per 2 pressure marks.

RESTORE: install a valid grounding model in pylon nine and complete 3 Grounding actions before 2 failures. One may be prepared from the labs. Each remaining Action uses DC 15 Arcana/Investigation or a concrete spell effect that establishes planar anchoring. Failure deals 2d6 force and adds one failure; at 2 failures Restore closes but Reform and Disconnect remain legal.

REFORM: establish three independent controls—student authorship audit, external ward review, emergency override. Each station is an Action and DC 15 Investigation/Insight/Persuasion or automatic with decisive evidence plus a willing authority. Three stations reconfigure the observatory so commencement never directly controls it again.

DISCONNECT: expose the observatory coupling after one deliberate disconnect action. Coupling AC 16, 28 HP, resistant to nonmagical weapon damage. Destroying it closes the breach and permanently severs commencement beacons from the observatory.

Initiative 20: Astral Shear. Two 15-foot zones shift orientation; creatures there make DC 15 Dexterity save or slide/fall 20 feet toward the aperture edge, stopping at ward railings unless already beyond them.

Directly reducing the Ninth Echo to 0 HP stabilizes the cycle temporarily but does not choose institutional outcome; the party must still spend one Action on Restore, Reform, or Disconnect to set the lasting state.

scenes.title: Resolution: Nine Names on the Ring
scenes.purpose: Reward restoring the missing work with correct authorship.
scenes.readAloud: The silver tear closes from the edges inward. When the dome turns blue again, nine names burn around the observatory ring. Mira Sol's is one of them. The graduates begin cheering only after someone removes Orien Pell's faculty crest from her old bay.
gmNotes: Award 300 gp total and four Ninefold Favor seals.
Mira's authorship is publicly restored and her expulsion reviewed.
The nine-capstone peer-review process remains but receives anti-substitution safeguards.

scenes.title: Resolution: Graduation Is Not a Control Panel
scenes.purpose: Reward structural reform rather than merely restoring one omitted slot.
scenes.readAloud: The observatory relights—but the nine commencement beacons do not. Their conduits now end at a new review dais where student, faculty, and outside warders each hold one key. The graduating class gets its ceremony back. The observatory gets a real safety process.
gmNotes: Award 325 gp total and the Independent Seal, granting advantage on one future Ninefold check involving academic records, magical review, or institutional procedure.
Commencement becomes symbolic; observatory cycling moves to a separate audited process.
Mira's authorship dispute is still recorded and adjudicated.

scenes.title: Resolution: The Sky Is No Longer Part of Graduation
scenes.purpose: Respect permanent disconnection while preserving the academy.
scenes.readAloud: The last coupling shatters. The observatory aperture closes like an eye. Outside, the nine graduation beacons remain standing—but they are only lights now. Students begin relighting them by hand, one at a time, with no planar machinery attached.
gmNotes: Award 300 gp total.
Commencement is permanently severed from observatory operations.
The academy may rebuild a separate observatory control system later under normal review.

encounters.name: The Ninth Echo
encounters.summary: The missing ninth ward input manifests as recursive planar force while the observatory opens to the Astral Sea.
encounters.resolution: Complete Restore, complete Reform, disconnect the observatory, or temporarily defeat the Echo then choose a lasting state.
encounters.talkOut: It accepts valid grounding and stable system states but does not negotiate institutional ethics.
encounters.bypass: Restore and Reform are full noncombat routes; Disconnect can be performed through object damage and control actions.
encounters.objective: Close the breach and set a durable observatory governance state.

pathPressure.principle: Level 9 utility magic can accelerate rescue and access, but evidence, grounding logic, and institutional end-state choices still matter.
prepared: A tested grounding model grants one prepared Restore success.
Rescuing all three lab jobs prevents extra Echo Fragments.
